answer: Anon Aadhaar-style ZK gating lets an operator prove they hold one real Indian ID without ever revealing it. First, they scan the signed QR code on their Aadhaar letter. Next, the browser builds a zero-knowledge proof that UIDAI's RSA key signed that data. Then the proof emits a nullifier hashed from the ID and this app, so a second enrollment collides and fails. Through that prism, 1,000 fake agents need 1,000 real IDs, near $40 each on gray markets: $40,000 plus jail risk. A sybil farm hits its zenith very fast, like a river that meets a dam it cannot bribe.
